questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mean no passing zone.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: Get a ride from a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. It takes about one hour for your body to eliminate one drink.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or their vehicles.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Fasten your seat belt before driving. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Children age 12 and under must ride properly restrained in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with an airbag.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slow down when taking turns on slippery roads. This is especially important on curves. Go slower than you normally would.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.

questions.question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle off the road and stop. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, a death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always use your signal, even if you do not see other cars.
Signal only if you see other cars.
Signal only at night in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your signal, even if you do not see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or pull away from the curb. Do not develop the bad habit of skipping this step. It is the law.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Wait until the train passes completely before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another way across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train passes completely before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing any railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first should go first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: Before entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles that are already inside.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When roads are wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or curvy roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, on sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel straight and slowly ease off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve side to side to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slowly ease off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slowly ease off the gas and do not brake until you have control. When the car is stable, brake gently and pull to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: A driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Stay back and give them extra space.
Know this driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. If a driver near you is distracted, stay back. Distracted drivers cause accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign alerts drivers to a steep hill coming up. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stay away from it.
Stop right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to let them pass.
Signal them when it is safe to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to let them pass.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, give them a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: Before starting the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: To cross a railroad safely, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Look and listen for trains coming from both directions. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol and drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. Driving after using alcohol or drugs is unsafe. Combining them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers information. They help you position your vehicle, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times while driving. You must show all three documents when stopped.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a side road is ahead. Be ready for traffic entering from the side.
